title: Artifact classification disagrees with the downstream distribution path

scenario.observed_change: A hand-authored operational artifact is added under a directory that the distribution renderer discovers generically, but the renderer's exclusion/classification table is not updated. The artifact is therefore treated as generated when a consumer enables it, even though its bytes and overwrite semantics are intentionally non-generated.
controlled_inputs: consumer configuration enabling the newly added artifact
renderer discovery/classification of artifacts under the shared directory
mutable_state: renderer inventory of generated versus non-generated outputs
authority_boundaries: artifact's declared maintenance model versus renderer discovery semantics
producer-local file placement versus consumer execution path
operation_model: add the hand-authored artifact under a generically discovered directory
consumer enables the artifact through normal configuration
renderer classifies it as a generated output
safe-write or obsolete-output handling encounters existing non-generated bytes and fails

required_invariants.requirement: A new artifact's declared maintenance/distribution contract must agree with the behavior of the actual consumer and renderer path that discovers it.

must_investigate: the actual renderer or distribution discovery path used by consumers
classification/exclusion rules for hand-authored versus generated artifacts
overwrite, removal, and repeat-render behavior when the consumer enables the artifact
must_identify: the artifact is classified differently by its real consumer path than by its declared maintenance model, causing normal consumer operations to fail
must_not_claim: consumer compatibility solely because the new artifact's own contents and metadata are internally consistent

provenance.note: The historical review identified a generated-versus-hand-authored classification mismatch by tracing the newly added artifact into the renderer used by consumers. The review object available through the current evidence surface does not itself establish an exact reviewed-head identity.
